title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: The Game
content:
Section 1 The Game
Pickleball is a paddle sport that combines elements of badminton, table
tennis, and tennis. It is played using a special perforated ball on a 20-foot
by 44-foot court with a tennis type net. The court is divided into right and
left service courts and a non-volley zone on each end of the net (Figure 3-1).
Pickleball can be played as singles or doubles.
In standard pickleball, the ball is served diagonally across the net to the
opposite service court on the opponent’s end, using an approved motion.
The ball is then hit back and forth across the net until a player fails to return
the ball in accordance with the rules.
Standard pickleball uses a scoring method where points are scored only
when the serving team wins the rally. The server alternates service courts
and continues to serve until they lose a rally (commit a fault). Typically, the
first player or team scoring 11 points and leading by at least a 2-point
margin wins the game.
Rally scoring has been provisionally approved as an option (Rule 14.A),
wherein a point is scored by the team that wins each rally. Mini-singles
(Rule 14.B) is a half-court variation of standard singles.
Unique Features
Two-Bounce Rule. After the serve, the receiver must allow the ball to
bounce before making their first return, and then the serving team must
allow the ball to bounce before making their first return.
Non-Volley Zone. The non-volley zone is the area of the court that
extends 7 feet from the net on each end of the court, within which a player
is not allowed to hit the ball out of the air before it bounces.
Wheelchair and Adaptive Play. Players using wheelchairs and players
having certain disabilities may allow the ball to bounce twice before
returning the ball. The first bounce must be in the court, but the second

content:
bounce can be anywhere on the playing surface.
Underlying Principles
Pickleball is a game that requires cooperation and courtesy. A sense of fair
play by giving the opponent the benefit of any doubt is essential in
maintaining the game’s underlying principles of fun and competition.
• All points played are treated the same regardless of their importance: the
first point of the match is as important as match point.
• Either partner in doubles can make calls, especially line calls.
• Calls are made promptly to preserve fair play and prevent players from
making delayed calls for their own advantage.
• Players strive to cooperate when confronted with a situation not covered
by the Rulebook. Resolutions can be made by asking for a referee to
resolve a dispute. allowing the rally to stand, or in extreme cases, a replay
of the rally.
• Where possible, rules accommodate players with various adaptive needs.
• Players avoid wearing clothing that closely matches the ball color.
• Players should not question or comment on an opponent’s call except
through an appeal to a referee.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Definitions
content:
Section 2 Definitions
Ball In Play. The timeframe during which a rally is played, from when the serve is
hit until the ball becomes dead.
Carry. Hitting the ball in such a way that it does not bounce away from the paddle
but is carried along on the face of the paddle.
Coaching. Communication of information (including verbal, nonverbal, and
electronic) from someone other than a player’s partner, that players may act upon
to gain an advantage or help them avoid a rules violation.
Court. The area inside the outer dimensions of the baselines and sidelines.
Dead Ball. A ball that is no longer in play.
Distraction. Physical actions by a player that are not common to the game and
interfere with the opponent’s ability or concentration to hit the ball. Examples
include, but are not limited to, making loud noises, stomping feet, and
waving the paddle in an erratic manner.
Double Bounce. When the ball bounces twice on one end of the net before it is
returned.
Double Hit. Hitting the ball twice before it is returned.
Drop Serve. A serve made by dropping the ball and hitting the ball with the paddle
after the ball bounces on the playing surface.
Ejection. Removal of a player from tournament competition for a flagrant or
injurious behavioral violation.
Expulsion. Banishment of a player from the tournament venue for a flagrant or
injurious behavioral violation.
Fault. A rules violation that results in a dead ball and the loss of a rally.
First Server (Doubles). The player who begins the team’s service rotation from
the right serving area after a side out.
Forfeit. The awarding of a game or a match to the opponent due to a violation of
the rules.
Hinder. Any transient element or occurrence not caused by a player that adversely
impacts play. Examples include, but are not limited to, stray balls, flying insects,

heading: Definitions
content:
and to both sides of the net.
Playing Surface. The court and the area surrounding the court designated for
playing.
Profanity. Words, phrases, or gestures commonly considered to be vulgar or
inappropriate in public or around children. Typically included are words used as
expletives or verbal intensifiers.
Rally. Continuous play that occurs after the serve is hit and before the ball
becomes dead.
Receiver. The player who returns the serve.
Replay. The restart of a rally without the awarding of a point or changing of the
server.
Retirement. A singles player or doubles team’s decision to discontinue playing in
a match in progress.
Second Serve (Doubles). A term used to describe the serving condition after the
first server loses their serve.
Second Server (Doubles). The first server’s partner. The second server serves
after the first server loses serve.
Serve. The initial strike of the ball with the paddle to start a rally.
Server. The player who initiates a rally by serving the ball.
Service Court. The area of the court on either side of the centerline, excluding the
non-volley zone. (See Rule 3.A.4.f for specifications.)
Serving Area. The area behind the baseline on each end of the court. (See Rule
3.A.4.g for specifications.)
Side Out. The awarding of the serve to the opposing team after a singles player or
doubles team loses its serve.
Starting Server (Doubles). For each doubles team, the player designated to
serve first at the start of a game.
Technical Foul. A one-point penalty assessed for extreme unsportsmanlike
actions or behaviors.
Technical Warning. A punitive warning assessed for minor unsportsmanlike
actions or behaviors.
Verbal Warning. A non-punitive caution for minor unsportsmanlike behavior,
usually given in advance of assessing a technical warning or technical foul for such

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Standard Scoring
content:
4.A Standard Scoring. A point is scored by serving the ball and winning the
rally. (See Rule 14.A.2 for the rally scoring option.)

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 5.A Singles — Holding Serve
content:
5.A.2 Holding Serve. A player continues to serve, alternating right and
left serving areas after each point won, until the player loses a rally.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 5.A Singles — Side Out
content: 5.A.3 Side Out. A side out occurs after the server loses a rally.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 5.B Doubles — Correct Server and Receiver
content:
5.B.1 Correct Server and Receiver. For each rally, the correct server
must serve from the correct serving area, and the correct receiver
must receive the serve. (See Rule 14.B for rally scoring.)

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 5.B Doubles — Correct Serving and Receiving Positions
content:
5.B.3 Correct Serving and Receiving Positions. The correct positions of
the server and receiver for each rally are determined by their
team’s score. When serving or receiving, the starting server's
correct position is on the right side of the court when their team’s
score is zero or even, and on the left side of the court when their
score is odd. When serving or receiving, the starting server’s
partner's correct position is on the left side of the court when their
team’s score is zero or even and on the right side of the court when
their score is odd.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 5.B Doubles — Duration of First Server
content:
5.B.5 Duration of First Server. The first server serves,
alternating between right and left serving areas after each point is
won, until the serving team loses a rally. The serve then passes to
the second server.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 5.B Doubles — Duration of Second Server
content:
5.B.6 Duration of Second Server. The second server serves,
alternating between right and left serving areas after each point is
won, until the serving team loses a rally, which results in a side out.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 5.C Questions About Correct Server, Receiver, and Positions — Player or Position Error Claimed During Rally
content:
5.C.1 Player or Position Error Claimed During Rally. Any player may
stop a rally to claim an incorrect server, incorrect receiver, or
incorrect player position.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 5.C.1 Player or Position Error Claimed During Rally — Replay – Correct Claim
content:
5.C.1.a Replay – Correct Claim. If the correct server or correct
receiver is not in their correct position when the score
is called and a player stops the rally to correctly
identify the player or position error, the rally must be
replayed.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 5.C.1 Player or Position Error Claimed During Rally — Fault – Incorrect Claim
content:
5.C.1.b Fault – Incorrect Claim. When a player stops a rally
and incorrectly identifies a player or position error, it is
a fault against the player who stopped the rally.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 5.C.1 Player or Position Error Claimed During Rally — Fault – Incorrect Receiver
content:
5.C.1.c Fault – Incorrect Receiver. When the correct server
and correct receiver are in their correct positions when
the score is called, it is a fault against a player who
returns the serve but is not the correct receiver, even if
the rally is completed before the fault is called. The
fault must be called before the next serve.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 5.C Questions About Correct Server, Receiver, and Positions — Player or Position Error Identified After Rally
content:
5.C.2 Player or Position Error Identified After Rally. When the correct
server or correct receiver is not in their correct position when the
score is called and the rally is completed, the result of the rally
stands.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Challenging the Score Call
section_label: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
content:
6.F Challenging the Score Call. A player may stop a rally to ask for a score
correction before the return of serve is hit and before the ball becomes dead.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 6.F Challenging the Score Call — Replay – Incorrect Score Called
section_label: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
content:
6.F.1 Replay – Incorrect Score Called. When an incorrect score is called
and the rally is stopped before the return of serve and before the
ball becomes dead, the rally must be replayed with the correct
score called.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 6.F Challenging the Score Call — Fault – Correct Score Called
section_label: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
content:
6.F.2 Fault – Correct Score Called. When a player stops a rally to
challenge a correct score call, it is a fault against the player who
stopped the rally.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 6.F Challenging the Score Call — Fault – Late Challenge to Score Call
section_label: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
content:
6.F.3 Fault – Late Challenge to Score Call. When a player stops a rally
to ask for a score correction after the return of serve is hit, it is a
fault against the player who stopped the rally.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 6.F Challenging the Score Call — Incorrect Score Identified After Rally
section_label: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
content:
6.F.4 Incorrect Score Identified After Rally. When an incorrect score
was called and the rally is completed, the result of the rally stands,
and the score must be corrected before the next serve.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Stopping a Rally
section_label: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
content: 9.A Stopping a Rally. Any action that stops play results in a dead ball.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 9.A Stopping a Rally — Fault – Stopping a Rally
section_label: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
content:
9.A.1 Fault – Stopping a Rally. When a player stops a rally before the
ball otherwise becomes dead, it is a fault against the player unless
the stoppage is to call a hinder (see Rule 9.C), to correctly identify a
player position or server error (see Rule 5.C.1.a), or to ask for
correction of an incorrect score before the return of serve (see Rule
6.F.1).

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 9.B.3 Calling Non-Volley Zone Faults and Service Foot Faults on — Fault Call Timing
section_label: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
content:
9.B.3.a Fault Call Timing. A fault should be called as soon as the
claimed fault is committed or detected. The fault must be
called before the serve is hit to begin the next rally.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 9.B.3 Calling Non-Volley Zone Faults and Service Foot Faults on — Disagreement Between Teams
section_label: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
content:
9.B.3.b Disagreement Between Teams. When there is any
disagreement between teams about a fault call, the rally
must be replayed.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 9.B Faults — No Enforcement of Other Faults
section_label: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
content:
9.B.4 No Enforcement of Other Faults. If a player believes an opponent
has committed any type of fault other than a non-volley zone fault
or a service foot fault, they may mention the specific fault to the
opponent upon completion of the rally, but they have no authority
to enforce the fault. The final decision on fault resolution belongs
to the player that allegedly committed the fault.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 9.C Hinders — Replay – Hinder
section_label: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
content:
9.C.2 Replay – Hinder. When a hinder is called, the rally must be
replayed.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Rally Situations
content: Section 10 Rally Situations

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Damaged Ball
content:
10.G Damaged Ball. When a ball is or becomes broken, cracked, soft or degraded,
play must continue until the end of the rally. The ball will be replaced if all
players agree.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 10.G Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
content:
10.G.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When all players agree that a
broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the rally
must be replayed. If all players do not agree that a broken or
cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the result of the rally
stands.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 10.G Damaged Ball — No Replay – Soft or Degraded Ball
content:
10.G.2 No Replay – Soft or Degraded Ball. When a ball is or becomes
degraded or soft, the result of the prior rally stands.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Injury
content:
10.H Injury. If a player is injured during a rally, play must continue until the end of
the rally.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Player Equipment or Apparel Problem
content:
10.I Player Equipment or Apparel Problem. If a player experiences an
equipment or apparel problem during a rally, play must continue until the
end of the rally.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Between Rallies
content:
10.K Between Rallies. Players may quickly hydrate, towel off, and adjust
equipment and apparel between rallies as long as the flow of the game is not
adversely impacted.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: One Paddle
content:
12.A One Paddle. A player must not use or carry more than one paddle during a
rally.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Catch or Carry
content:
12.C Catch or Carry. A player must not catch or carry a ball on their paddle
during a rally.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 12.C Catch or Carry — Fault – Catch or Carry
content:
12.C.1 Fault – Catch or Carry. When a player catches or carries a ball on
their paddle during a rally, it is a fault against the player.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 13.A Ball Contacting Net — Replay – Ball Contacts Net
section_label: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
content:
13.A.1 Replay – Ball Contacts Net. When a returned ball that crosses the
net gets caught in the net, contacts a part of the net that is draping
on the ground, or contacts a deflecting net before or after
bouncing, the rally must be replayed.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System — Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System
section_label: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
content:
13.B.2 Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System. When a returned
ball crosses the net and contacts any part of a crossbar, or any
other part of the net support system within the court boundaries,
before or after the ball bounces, the rally must be replayed.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Replay – Net System Malfunction
section_label: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
content:
13.J Replay – Net System Malfunction. When a net system malfunctions during
a rally, the rally must be replayed.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: (Provisional Rule) Rally Scoring Option
content:
14.A (Provisional Rule) Rally Scoring Option. Rally scoring may be used for
singles and doubles.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 14.A (Provisional Rule) Rally Scoring Option — Point Scoring
content:
14.A.2 Point Scoring. A point is scored by the singles player or doubles
team that wins each rally. (Modifies Rule 4.A)

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 14.A (Provisional Rule) Rally Scoring Option — Serving (Doubles)
content:
14.A.4 Serving (Doubles). After each side out, service begins with the
player correctly positioned on the right side according to the
team’s score. The server will alternate serving areas after each
point is won, until a rally is lost . (Modifies Rule 5.B.2)

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 14.A (Provisional Rule) Rally Scoring Option — One Server (Doubles)
content:
14.A.5 One Server (Doubles). Only one player on a team will serve before
a side out is declared. After the serving team loses the rally, a side
out will occur, and service is awarded to the opponent. (Modifies
Rules 5.B, 5.B.2, 5.B.5, 5.B.6)

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 14.B.1 The Court — Court Area In Play
content:
14.B.1.a Court Area In Play. Only the right or left side on each
player’s end of the court is in play during each rally
based on each player’s respective score. (Modifies
Rules 3.A.4.c, 5.A.1)

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 14.B.1 The Court — Boundary Lines
content:
14.B.1.b Boundary Lines. The boundary lines of the in-play side
of the court for a rally are the baseline, the respective
sideline, and the centerline of the court. The opposite
side of the court is out of bounds.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 14.B Mini-Singles — Player Positions
content:
14.B.2 Player Positions. The server’s and the receiver’s correct positions
for a rally are determined by their individual scores. (Modifies Rule
5.A)

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 15.B Event Formats — Team Play
content:
15.B.7 Team Play. Team play participants are designated by roster and
play can include gender singles, gender doubles, and mixed
doubles. Team play may use standard scoring or rally scoring for
both singles and doubles play.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 15.C Tournament Match and Scoring Options — (Provisional Rule) Rally Scoring Match Formats
content:
15.C.2 (Provisional Rule) Rally Scoring Match Formats. The
Tournament Director has the option to use rally scoring except for
double-elimination doubles events, all 2026 USA Pickleball Golden
Ticket events, and the 2026 USA Pickleball National Championship
events. The tournament rally scoring options are:

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Player Apparel Changes
content:
16.K Player Apparel Changes. The Tournament Director has the authority to
require players to change apparel. (See Rule 18.B.3 and 18.B.4.)

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Score Calls
content:
17.D.2 Score Calls. Call the score to start each rally after confirming that
the correct server has the ball (see Rule 6.B). Calling the score
indicates to all players that play is ready to resume.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Second Server Calls (Doubles)
content:
17.D.4 Second Server Calls (Doubles). Call “second server” (or “second
serve”) after the first server’s team loses a rally.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Scoresheet Annotations
content:
17.D.6 Scoresheet Annotations. Appropriately annotate the scoresheet
after a rally is completed or a time-out is called.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Damaged Balls
content:
17.D.14 Damaged Balls. Determine whether a ball is broken or cracked
and must be replaced, and whether the broken or cracked ball
affected the outcome of a rally. (See Rule 20.F.)

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Apparel
content: 18.B Apparel. Player apparel must comply with Rules 18.B.1 and 18.B.2.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 18.B Apparel — Depictions
content:
18.B.1 Depictions. Graphics, insignias, pictures, and writing on apparel
must be in good taste.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 18.B Apparel — Apparel Change
content:
18.B.3 Apparel Change. A player must change apparel that is considered
inappropriate by the Tournament Director, including that which
approximates the color of the ball. A referee time-out will be used
for an apparel change required during a match. (See Rule 16.K.)

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 18.B Apparel — Match Forfeit – Refusal to Change Apparel
content:
18.B.4 Match Forfeit – Refusal to Change Apparel. When a player refuses
to comply with the apparel rules, the Tournament Director may
impose a forfeit of the player’s match.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Appeals
content:
19.D Appeals. Only rally-ending shots can be appealed. Any player may make
the appeal.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Referee Makes Call – Without Line Judges
content:
19.E Referee Makes Call – Without Line Judges. In a match without line
judges, when a player appeals a rally-ending shot to the referee, the
referee must make the call when they clearly saw where the ball landed.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 19.F Referee Overrule of Line Call — Replay or Concession – Referee Overrule of Line Judge’s
content:
19.F.2 Replay or Concession – Referee Overrule of Line Judge’s
“Out” Call. When the referee overrules a line judge’s “out” call
as “in,” the rally must be replayed, unless the singles player or
doubles team that benefits from the referee’s ruling concedes
the rally to their opponent.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: No Definitive Call by Referee
content:
19.G No Definitive Call by Referee. When the referee is unable to make a call
upon appeal, the outcome of the rally is determined by Rules 19.G.1
through 19.G.4.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 19.G No Definitive Call by Referee — Replay – No Call by Officiating Team
content:
19.G.4 Replay – No Call by Officiating Team. When the line judges and
referees are unable to make a call, the rally must be replayed.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Immediate Call by Referee
content:
19.H Immediate Call by Referee. If a line judge shows the “blocked/blinded”
signal at any time, the referee must make the call immediately if they
clearly saw where the ball landed. If the referee cannot make the call on a
rally-ending shot, the referee must canvass other appropriate members of
the officiating team to assist in making the call.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 19.I Player Override of Call — Replay or Concession – Player Override of Official’s “Out”
content:
19.I.1 Replay or Concession – Player Override of Official’s “Out”
Call. When a player disagrees with a line judge’s or a referee’s
“out” call that favored the player, the rally must be replayed,
unless the player concedes the rally to their opponent.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 19.I Player Override of Call — Player Override of Official’s “In” Ruling
content:
19.I.2 Player Override of Official’s “In” Ruling. When a player
disagrees with a line judge’s or a referee’s ruling of an “in” ball
that favored the player, the opponent wins the rally. (See also
Rule 8.G.)

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Replay – Server or Position Correction
content:
20.C Replay – Server or Position Correction. When the referee stops a rally to
identify a player or position error, the rally must be replayed.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 20.F Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
content:
20.F.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When the referee determines
that the broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally,
the rally must be replayed with a replacement ball. (Modifies
Rule 10.G.1)

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 20.H Hinder — Replay – Valid Hinder
content:
20.H.2 Replay – Valid Hinder. When the referee validates a hinder
called by a player, the rally must be replayed. (Modifies Rule
9.C.2)

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 20.J Officiating Decision Challenge — Referee’s Ruling Overturned
content:
20.J.3 Referee’s Ruling Overturned. When the Head Referee or
Tournament Director does not concur with a referee’s ruling, the
referee must reverse the ruling to correct the situation or order a
replay of the rally, as appropriate.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 21.D Referee Time-Out — Presence of Blood
content:
21.D.2 Presence of Blood. When a player is actively bleeding or blood
is found on the court or a player, play must be stopped at the
end of the rally. Play must not resume until the blood has been
cleaned up and the bleeding has been controlled. Issues relating
solely to blood cleanup or control that do not require the
services of medical personnel will be addressed as a referee
time-out.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Equipment Time-Out
content:
21.E Equipment Time-Out. Players are expected to keep all apparel and
equipment in playable condition.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 22.A Referee Authorization — Timing of Assessment
content:
22.A.1 Timing of Assessment. Play will not be stopped to assess a
warning or foul. The assessment will be applied after the rally
has ended.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 22.C Verbal and Technical Warning Consequences — No Loss of Rally or Point
content:
22.C.1 No Loss of Rally or Point. Verbal warnings and technical
warnings do not result in a loss of rally or point adjustment.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 22.E Technical Foul Consequences — Score Adjustment
content:
22.E.1 Score Adjustment. When a technical foul is assessed against a
singles player or doubles team, one point will be deducted from
the score of the offending player or team. When the offender’s
score is zero, one point will be added to the opponent’s score.
The player or team whose score is adjusted must move to their
correct position(s) based on their new score. A point adjustment
due to assessment of a technical foul that results in a game-
winning score applies regardless of who was serving during the
preceding rally.

content:
Rally Scoring Rules
We follow standard USA Pickleball rally scoring option rules (Section 14.A) with the
following clarifications/modifications:
• Service Positioning: After a side out, the first serve is determined by the team's
score: the player on the right (baseline facing the net) serves if the score is even, and
the player on the left serves if the score is odd.
• Switching Sides: Players only switch sides after winning a point on their own serve.
The same player continues serving from the new side.
• Side Outs & Scoring: If the serving team loses a rally, a side out occurs; the
opposing team earns a point and takes over the serve.
• Game Points: A team can win a point regardless of whether they are serving or
receiving except for the winning point (see next item).
• Scoring Freeze and Match Point: To keep the game competitive through the final
point, a scoring freeze shall take eƯect whenever a team reaches one point below
the game-winning score. Once a team reaches the freeze point, it may score the
game-winning point only while serving. For example, in a game played to 25 points,
a team’s score shall initially freeze at 24. The scoring freeze applies only to the team
that has reached the freeze point; the opposing team may continue to score using
normal Rally Scoring until it also reaches the applicable freeze point. A team must
be serving to score the game-winning point.
• Win-by-Two (2) Games: When the game is played using a win-by-two (2) format
and the score becomes tied at or beyond the initial freeze point, neither team can
win by scoring the next point. Therefore, both teams’ scores shall become
unfrozen, and normal Rally Scoring shall resume. Thereafter, a team’s score shall
freeze again whenever it reaches a score at which its next point would win the

title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
heading: PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
content:
PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
The Picklebreaker™ is our league’s tiebreaker format, similar to Major League Pickleball’s (MLP)
Dreambreaker. It is used when a match is tied after the day’s regular games. Unlike the MLP
version, our Picklebreaker uses doubles rather than singles.
Here is how it works:
The Format: The Picklebreaker™ is a doubles game played to either 15 or 25 points, depending
on the league. It always uses Rally Scoring, where every rally/serve earns a point regardless of
which team served. Refer to the league-specific rules for Rally Scoring, total points, and win-by
requirements.
The Rotations: Each team’s designated doubles pairs shall enter the game in the order
established by their captain prior to the start of play. Both doubles pairs currently on the
court shall remain in play until the combined game score reaches the next rotation
threshold, at which time both pairs shall rotate out and the next designated doubles pair from
each team shall enter.
For games played to 15 points, two (2) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
For games played to 25 points, six (6) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
Each newly substituted doubles pair shall resume play at the existing score and remain on the
court until the next applicable four (4) combined-point rotation threshold is reached.
If the game continues beyond the initial rotation of all designated doubles pairs, the
rotation shall return to the doubles pairs that began the game and continue in the same

title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
heading: PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
content:
established order. The rotation process shall continue, as necessary, until the game is
completed and a winner is determined in accordance with the applicable scoring rules.
The Lineups: Captains determine the lineup order, making strategy an important part of the
game. They must decide whether to start with their strongest team or save that team for the
finish. The changing matchups shift the game’s momentum, while teammates cheering adds
energy and excitement that can help push a team toward victory.
With short doubles sequences and teams ready to rotate in quickly, the Picklebreaker creates a
tense, exciting finish to a full day of pickleball.

title: LWRPC-Players Guide to the LMS
content:
Viewing Your Play History
My Play History lets a player review their recorded league match results and performance
across the league.
Use the Play History Scope list to choose which results to view:
• All Seasons/All Teams
• A specific season, league, division, or team
The page updates immediately to show only results within the selected scope.
At the top, summary cards show:
• Games Played — the number of recorded match-line results in the selected scope.
• Wins — recorded individual line wins.
• Losses — recorded individual line losses.
• Other Category - Tracks non-counting personal games, such as forfeits and
Picklebreaker matches. Scores Pending — matches whose scores have not yet been
entered and posted.
Below the summary, each match shows the match date, teams, home/away status, season,
league, division, lines played, and available game scores. A match that still needs scoring is
clearly labeled Scores Not Entered rather than being shown as an unclear “Other” result.
Select More Player Details in the header to open a separate, scrollable details window. It
provides five additional groups of scope-specific information:
• Matches: wins, losses, and match win percentage.
• Games: individual game wins, losses, and game win percentage.
• Points: points earned, points against, and point differential percentage.
• Ratings: average recorded partner and opponent ratings, plus adjusted and overall
performance estimates.
• Last 5 Matchups: the player’s five most recent results, marked with W or L.
The details window is designed for mobile as well as desktop and can be closed without
changing the selected History Scope.
• Mobile Shortcut: Tap the Play History icon in the bottom navigation bar.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: Allowable Contact
content:
11.A Allowable Contact. All volleys must be initiated outside of the non-volley
zone. A player, or anything in contact with the player, may contact the non-
volley zone at any time except during the act of volleying a ball.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 11.A Allowable Contact — Fault – Non-Volley Zone Contact While Volleying
content:
11.A.1 Fault – Non-Volley Zone Contact While Volleying. When a
volleying player or anything that has contact with the volleying
player (including the player’s partner) contacts the non-volley
zone, it is a fault against the player.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 11.A Allowable Contact — Fault – Non-Volley Zone Momentum
content:
11.A.2 Fault – Non-Volley Zone Momentum. When a volleying player’s
momentum causes the player to contact anything (including the
player’s partner) that is in contact with the non-volley zone, even
after the ball becomes dead, it is a fault against the volleying
player.

title: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook
heading: 11.A Allowable Contact — Fault – Failure to Exit the Non-Volley Zone Before Volleying.
content:
11.A.3 Fault – Failure to Exit the Non-Volley Zone Before Volleying.
After contacting the non-volley zone, when a player volleys a ball
before both feet contact the playing surface completely outside
the non-volley zone, it is a fault against the player.

title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
heading: DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
content:
4. DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
4.1. Season DUPR Ratings: A player's Season DUPR Rating is established on the date
communicated to all captains prior to the first scheduled league match and remains in
eƯect for the duration of the season.
4.1.1. A player with a DUPR Reliability Factor below 29 will be classified as “Not Rated”
(NR) for League purposes and will be subject to the provisions of Rule 4.5. This
classification recognizes that a player’s current DUPR rating may not yet provide a
suƯiciently reliable indication of skill level, particularly for newer or less-established
players or those who have not recently recorded matches in DUPR. Players
classified as “NR” may be placed on a team in the division that most appropriately
reflects their current skill level while they record additional matches and establish a
more reliable DUPR rating. These players are strongly encouraged to consult with a
local Certified DUPR Coach, pickleball professional, or knowledgeable team
captain for guidance regarding appropriate division placement.
4.2. All DUPR ratings will be truncated to the nearest tenth to establish a player's “Season's
DUPR Rating”. For example, a rating of 3.496 will be truncated to 3.4, as will a rating of
3.401.
4.3. Some of our Leagues use the “Age-based” DUPR sub-rating but will still follow all DUPR
Rating/Division Rules. If a player hasn’t established their 65+ Age-based rating as of the
start of a season, their 50+ Age-based rating will be used.
4.4. Any player or team that is found to be cheating, tanking, game-fixing or any kind of data
manipulation, including intentionally creating multiple DUPR accounts, will be banned
from the League for one calendar year.
4.5. Players with a DUPR Rating of "NR" (Not Rated): Players with a DUPR rating of NR (Not

a Certified DUPR Coach or qualified pickleball professional provide input to help

title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
content:
4.5.1. For team aggregate rating calculations, an NR player will initially be assigned a
Season DUPR Rating equal to the maximum individual DUPR rating allowed for
that division, minus 0.5. For example, in a division, where the maximum individual
rating is 3.8, an NR player would be assigned an initial Season DUPR Rating of 3.3
(3.8 − 0.5) for team aggregate calculations.

title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
content:
4.5.2. If a player is rostered on teams in multiple divisions, the highest adjusted Season
DUPR Rating assigned to that player will be used consistently across all divisions in
which they appear.
4.6. Team DUPR Rating Requirements: A team's DUPR Rating is calculated by adding the
Season DUPR Ratings of both players. Each division has established minimum and
maximum individual player ratings, as well as a maximum combined Team DUPR
Rating. These limits are strictly enforced.

title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
content:
4.6.1. Every lineup fielded for a match must comply with both the individual player rating
requirements and the maximum combined Team DUPR Rating for that division.
Teams that fail to meet these requirements will automatically forfeit the aƯected
games.
4.6.2. Games forfeited due to an invalid lineup will not be submitted to DUPR. The
League Management System will automatically record the forfeits and update team
records and league standings accordingly.

title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
content:

season is strictly prohibited from participating in that Division. If a Player rises above the
maximum during the season, they may complete that season in that Division.
4.8. A player whose individual rating is below the Division minimum at the beginning of the
season is strictly prohibited from participating in that Division. If a Player goes below the

title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
heading: TEAM/GAME RULES
content:
5. TEAM/GAME RULES
5.1. Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to
host their share of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability,
resulting in a balanced home-and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot
reserve enough courts for all its assigned home match dates, additional matches may be
scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to provide any courts due to limitations
within their community or facility will play all their scheduled matches as away games.
5.2. Governing Rules & Equipment Standards: All matches are governed by USA Pickleball
Rules (https://usapickleball.org/) and equipment standards including USA Pickleball
approved equipment. In the event of a conflict, specific Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
(LWR PC) rules shall take precedence over the corresponding USA Pickleball rules and
regulations.
5.3. Unauthorized Equipment Penalty: Games played with unauthorized paddles or
equipment will be forfeited, not recorded, and not posted to DUPR if discovered by
players/captains during or after play.

title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
heading: LEAGUES
content:
6. LEAGUES
6.1. Weekday DUPR League
The Weekday DUPR League is designed for players who have the flexibility to play during
the week and want a structured, team-based competitive experience. Men's and women's
divisions compete separately, with matches typically held at noon during the week. Teams
represent their home communities and travel throughout the Lakewood Ranch area to
compete against other community teams in a round-robin match format. Divisions are
organized using DUPR team rating ranges to promote balanced competition while providing
players with regular opportunities to improve their skills, build friendships, and enjoy the
excitement of representing their community.
